subject: Escalation: Northpeak asking for higher throughput guarantee (Dedicated)
body:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Escalation: Northpeak asking for higher throughput guarantee (Dedicated)

Lauren (cc Steph) — need a quick decision today.

Northpeak is asking us to *write* a higher throughput guarantee than the Premium tier draft for their Dedicated deployment. They’re framing it as a gating procurement item (“we can’t take it to legal unless it’s in the order form / SLO schedule”).

What they’re asking for (in plain English): a minimum sustained throughput floor that’s ~30–40% above our current Premium guarantee assumptions, plus language that it applies during their “business hours peak” (which is basically their whole day).

I’m aligned that we should avoid bespoke promises, but this one is coming in as an exec escalation on their side and we’re in a competitive bake-off.

Questions:
1) Do we have a hard policy to say “no above tier” and push them to bigger shape / more nodes instead?
2) If we do make an exception, what’s the required approvals + pricing uplift guidance? (Deal desk style.)
3) What’s the risk posture: can we offer this as a *burst* commitment with throttling / admission control and carve-outs, vs a true guarantee with credits?

I’m forwarding the actual ask below.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
GTM Sponsor, Redwood Inference


---------- Forwarded message ----------
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 8:47 AM PST
Subject: Fwd: Re: Dedicated throughput guarantee language
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>

FYI — this is the email that triggered it.


Begin forwarded message:

From: Maya Chen <maya@northpeak.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, Feb 18, 2025 at 6:22 PM PST
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput guarantee language

Stephanie — thanks again for the deep dive last week.

We’re aligned on Dedicated, but we need the throughput commitment stated more clearly and at the level we discussed verbally. Our team is budgeting and staffing around a minimum floor, not “best effort.”

Specifically, we need:
- A minimum sustained throughput commitment for our deployment (aggregate), measured over a rolling window (we’re fine with 10–15 min), that reflects our expected traffic (mix of short + medium prompts).
- This commitment should be written into the SLO schedule / order form.
- If Redwood can’t meet it, we need a defined remedy (service credit).

We are evaluating another provider who will commit to a higher minimum. If Redwood can match, we can move forward this month.

Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide this (and share the exact language)?

Thanks,
Maya

—
Maya Chen
Head of Platform
Northpeak AI



From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 10:03 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Northpeak asking for higher throughput guarantee (Dedicated)

We should not write bespoke above-tier minimums into the order form as a default. The whole point of the tier project is to make the commitment measurable and enforceable *without* one-off exceptions.

That said, there’s a path if we decide it’s worth it:

Policy (proposed, consistent with what we’ve been aligning on internally):
- Tier guarantees are the only “standard” guarantees.
- Any above-tier commitment requires: Product (me) + SRE signoff + Infra capacity signoff.
- The commitment must include workload assumptions (prompt length distribution bounds, max context, streaming on/off) and explicit exclusions (maintenance, customer-side backpressure, retries, etc.).
- If they want higher minimum throughput, the cleanest solution is: bigger shape / more nodes = higher aggregate throughput. We guarantee at the tier level per deployment/shape, not as an unbounded number.

Commercial guidance (if we do exception):
- Price uplift is required. Otherwise we’re eating both the capacity risk and the SLA remedy risk.
- Remedy needs to be constrained (credits capped; no termination right tied to throughput; must reference our measurement standard).

What I need from you/Steph to decide:
1) What’s their concrete target number, and what shape are we proposing today?
2) Are they asking for a guarantee that ignores admission control (i.e., they can send unlimited concurrency)? If yes, we should say no.
3) What’s the close date / competitive context and what’s the committed spend?

If you can send me the target and current proposal shape, I can respond with either:
(A) hold line: “Premium tier guarantee + recommend larger shape” or
(B) exception: “custom throughput addendum” with tight assumptions + uplift.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Product, Dedicated (DRI)


From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 10:39 AM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Northpeak asking for higher throughput guarantee (Dedicated)

Got it.

Answers (as best as we have right now):
1) Target: they’re asking for ~30–40% above the Premium floor we described in the last call. They didn’t give a single number in writing yet; it came verbally + they’re now pushing us to “match what we discussed.”
2) They absolutely assume they can run high concurrency at peak. They have an internal queue, but their expectation is “no throttling unless something is broken.”
3) Close date: they want to send to procurement/legal this week. Competitive: yes (they named another provider willing to commit higher minimums). Spend: meaningful (Steph can confirm exact).

Proposed path from GTM side:
- We push “bigger shape” as the way to get higher sustained throughput and keep the guarantee standard.
- If they insist on a number above tier, we offer it only as: bounded workload + bounded concurrency + admission control + capped credits.

Lauren — can you give us language we can send today that positions this clearly (and doesn’t sound like we’re dodging)?

Also: if we go the exception route, what uplift range should I anchor? (e.g., +20–30%?)

— Jordan


From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, Feb 19, 2025 at 12:14 PM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Northpeak asking for higher throughput guarantee (Dedicated)

Adding details:

- Current proposal is Dedicated Premium in us-west.
- Their stated usage: mixed prompt sizes, heavy daytime peak, some streaming.
- They are sensitive to anything that looks like “we can throttle you.” They want to tell their product teams that capacity is locked.
- Competitive note: they are comparing vs “a dedicated H100 cluster” elsewhere with a high minimum commitment (they won’t share how it’s measured).
- Timing: they want to start redlines next week; decision end of month.

On pricing: if we go above-tier + remedy in writing, I agree we need an uplift. My guess is we can hold them at +25% without losing the deal, but if we come back with +50% they’ll likely walk.

We also need crisp language on measurement assumptions. They keep asking “does your guarantee hold if our prompts spike?”

— Steph
Stephanie Nguyen
Sales Enablement, Redwood Inference


From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, Feb 20, 2025 at 4:28 PM PST
Subject: Re: Escalation: Northpeak asking for higher throughput guarantee (Dedicated)

Here’s what we should do.

Recommendation: hold the line on tiers, offer higher aggregate throughput via more capacity.
- We can credibly commit to Premium tier throughput *as defined by our standard*.
- If they want +30–40% more sustained throughput, the correct mechanism is adding capacity (bigger shape and/or additional replicas) with the same tier commitment, not rewriting the commitment.
- This keeps us out of a “promise a number, then fight about measurement” trap.

Customer-facing language (OK to send):
“Redwood Dedicated throughput commitments are standardized by tier and tied to a defined measurement methodology. If you require higher sustained throughput than the Premium tier floor for your workload, we can meet that by sizing the deployment appropriately (larger hardware shape and/or additional replicas) while keeping the commitment enforceable and supportable. We can also share the measurement definition and the workload assumptions required for the commitment to apply.”

If they insist on a bespoke above-tier commitment:
- We only do it with (a) explicit workload bounds (max context length, prompt/response length distribution bands, streaming behavior), (b) explicit max concurrency / admission control policy, and (c) credits capped and conditioned on compliance with those assumptions.
- Commercial: I’m aligned with anchoring +25–30% uplift minimum, because this is effectively us selling both capacity risk and SLA risk.

If you want to go exception route, I’ll need you to confirm:
- the exact language they want in the SLO schedule
- whether they’ll accept an admission control statement (they need to agree that throttling is expected behavior in overload vs an SLA breach)

I did a quick skim of the redlines attachment Steph added — they’re trying to remove most carve-outs. That’s a hard no.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Product, Dedicated (DRI)
Redwood Inference
